message.content: In lions, one of the most noticeable dominant traits is the presence of a mane in adult males. The gene that controls mane development is inherited in a dominant fashion—if a male lion inherits the dominant allele from either parent, it will develop a mane. This trait is not present in females (they lack the dominant allele), and it is a clear example of dominance in a natural population.
